issues.failure_explanation: The proof concludes with exponent (d+1)^T = (2q+2)^T, but the theorem statement and the known convergence order of the degree d=2q+1 Padé/Newton-Schulz iteration use exponent (q+1)^T. The stronger bound with (d+1)^T is false, so the proof as written does not establish the stated theorem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (d+1)^T by (q+1)^T throughout the convergence proof so that it matches the theorem statement and the cited Padé iteration rate.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the convergence rate for Polar Express is invalid as written; the stated bound remains true but is not supported by the given proof.
issues.title: Incorrect exponent in convergence proof
issues.why_classification: The theorem statement is correct and a one-line exponent correction restores the proof without changing the mathematical content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let the image of $f$ on $[\ell,u]$ be $[a,b]$. We will prove that $\frac{a}{b} \leq \frac{\ell_T}{u_T}$  by contradiction.

issues.failure_explanation: The induction step considers an arbitrary composition f and lets its image be [a,b]. If a,b are both negative, the displayed formula for the error of cf is wrong (the maximum error becomes (b-a)/|a+b|), and a/b can exceed \ell_T/u_T. Such f cannot be competitive because the final odd polynomial maps negative values to negative values, giving error at least 1, but the proof does not exclude or handle this case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a short case argument: any T-step composition that could beat the greedy composition must have f(x)>0 on [\ell,u]; otherwise the last odd polynomial produces negative values and error \ge 1, while the greedy composition has error < 1. Then the existing algebra applies.
issues.overall_effect: The induction proof of Theorem greedy is incomplete for compositions whose image on [\ell,u] lies entirely in negative numbers.
issues.title: Missing negative-image case in greedy optimality proof
issues.why_classification: The missing case is easily excluded by a local observation, and the theorem statement itself remains correct.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem greedy guarantees optimality for polynomials that minimize over [\ell_t,u_t] without modification. The algorithm alg:polarexpress instead minimizes over [max(\ell_t,u_t/10),u_t] (cushioning) and then applies a safety factor p_t(\cdot/1.01). These are not the optimal polynomials of Theorem greedy, so the algorithm as written does not inherit the theorem's worst-case optimality guarantee. The paper acknowledges these as finite-precision tweaks with negligible practical effect, but the formal guarantee is for the unmodified method.

failure_location.quote: Our algorithm first computes the polynomials $p_1,\ldots,p_{T}$ of \Cref{theorem:greedy} in full precision using the Remez algorithm.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Clarify that the optimality guarantee applies to the idealized algorithm using the unmodified greedy polynomials, and that alg:polarexpress is a finite-precision heuristic modification whose optimality is not formally guaranteed.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised worst-case optimality guarantee does not formally apply to the practical Polar Express algorithm described in alg:polarexpress.
issues.title: Optimality guarantee does not apply to the stated algorithm
issues.why_classification: The central theoretical guarantee is detached from the implemented algorithm; restoring a formal guarantee would require either removing the tweaks or proving a new bound for the modified construction.
